clauses.reason: The sole clause abolishes the Typhus Commission as of June 30, 1946 and directs liquidation of its affairs under the Secretary of War. The stated date is an own-terms effective date for the abolition (signing January 17, 1946), so the first end is June 30, 1946; the order does not use an "until" formulation, so no inclusive/exclusive reading arises. No held source shows an earlier abolition or a later extension. The ending source is the held original text of the order, which contains the clause.

research_rationale:
EO 9680 (January 17, 1946) abolished the United States of America Typhus Commission, established by EO 9285 of December 24, 1942, and directed the Secretary of War to supervise its liquidation. The order states the abolition is as of June 30, 1946, a date fixed by its own terms, and has a single paragraph of operative text (abolition) plus a liquidation direction. The status is NO: by its own terms the commission was abolished as of June 30, 1946, a self-executing abolition, and no held source revives it. The ending source is the order's own operative text; the creating order EO 9285 is the held record that identifies the body abolished.

savings.reason: The order itself provides that the liquidation of the commission's affairs and the disposition of its records and scientific data are to be accomplished under the supervision of the Secretary of War; that residual liquidation function is carried by the Secretary of War and is the only savings-type provision in the order. Bounded searches of the U.S. Code, eCFR and OFR catalog found no continuing reliance on EO 9680.
